title.zh: 卷一百四十七 志9: 刑法志
title.raw: 卷一百四十七 志9: 刑法志 Volume 147: Treatises 9 Punishment and Law

sentences.zh: 刑法志

translations.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law
translations.idiomatic: Monograph on Criminal Law

sentences.zh: （案：《刑法志序》，《永樂大典》原闕。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: The preface to the Treatise on Punishment and Law is missing in the original Yongle Encyclopedia.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Editorial note: The preface to this monograph was absent in the Yongle Encyclopedia source.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁太祖開平三年十一月，詔太常卿李燕、御史蕭頃、中書舍人張兗、戶部侍郎崔沂、大理卿王鄯、刑部郎中崔誥，共刪定律令格式。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Kaiping under Liang Taizu, an edict ordered Grand Master of Ceremonies Li Yan, Censor Xiao Huan, Secretariat Drafter Zhang Chong, Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Yi, Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Wang Shan, and Secretary in the Ministry of Punishments Cui Gao jointly to revise and abridge the statutes, ordinances, regulations, and formats.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kaiping year 3 (909), Emperor Taizu of Liang ordered Li Yan as grand master of ceremonies, Xiao Huan as censor, Zhang Chong as secretariat drafter, Cui Yi as vice minister of revenue, Wang Shan as chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, and Cui Gao as a secretary in the Ministry of Punishments to jointly revise the corpus of statutes, ordinances, administrative regulations, and procedural formats.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，宰臣薛貽矩奏：「太常卿李燕等重刊定律令三十卷，式二十卷，格一十卷，並目錄一十三卷，律疏三十卷，凡五部一十帙，共一百三卷。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year, Chief Minister Xue Yiju memorialized: "Grand Master of Ceremonies Li Yan and others have newly engraved and fixed the statutes and ordinances in thirty scrolls, regulations in twenty scrolls, formats in ten scrolls, together with tables of contents in thirteen scrolls, and commentaries on the statutes in thirty scrolls—five sections in ten fascicles, totaling one hundred three scrolls."
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the following year, chief minister Xue Yiju reported that Li Yan’s commission had produced a newly engraved set: thirty scrolls of statutes and ordinances, twenty of regulations, ten of formats, thirteen of tables of contents, and thirty of statutory commentary—five parts bound in ten fascicles, 103 scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 敕中書舍人李仁儉詣閣門奉進，伏請目為《大梁新定格式律令》，仍頒下施行。

translations.literal: An imperial order commanded Secretariat Drafter Li Renjian to proceed to the Gate of Credentials and present them with reverence, requesting that they be titled "Newly Fixed Formats, Statutes, and Ordinances of the Great Liang" and still be promulgated for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then directed secretariat drafter Li Renjian to present the completed codes at the Gate of Credentials and asked that they be formally named the Newly Fixed Formats, Statutes, and Ordinances of the Great Liang and put into effect throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the request.

sentences.zh: （原註：是時，大理卿李保殷進所撰《刑律總要》十二卷。）〉

translations.literal: (Original note: At this time Grand Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Li Baoyin presented his compiled "General Summary of Criminal Statutes" in twelve scrolls.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Marginal note: At the same time Li Baoyin, chief judge of the Court of Judicial Review, submitted his own twelve-scroll General Summary of Criminal Statutes.)〉

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗同光元年十二月，御史臺奏：「當司刑部、大理寺本朝法書，自朱溫僭逆，刪改事條，或重貨財，輕入人命，或自徇枉過，濫加刑罰。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Tongguang under Tang Zhuangzong, the Censorate memorialized: "The Ministry of Punishments of this office and the Court of Judicial Review—this dynasty's legal texts—since Zhu Wen's usurpation, had their provisions revised and deleted, in some cases valuing property heavily while lightly treating human life, or indulging wrongful excess and wantonly adding penalties.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Tongguang year 1 (923), the Censorate reported that the Tang Ministry of Punishments and Court of Judicial Review had once possessed the dynasty’s authentic law books, but after Zhu Wen’s rebellion those texts were altered—sometimes making goods weigh more than lives, sometimes letting personal bias inflate punishments.

sentences.zh: 今見在三司收貯刑書，並是偽廷刪改者，兼偽廷先下諸道追取本朝法書焚毀，或經兵火所遺，皆無舊本節目。

translations.literal: The penal texts now held in storage by the three offices are all versions revised by the false court; moreover the false court had earlier sent orders to the various circuits to seize and burn this dynasty's law books, or what survived war and fire is all without the old section headings.
translations.idiomatic: Every penal code still archived in the three judicial offices was a Liang revision, and the usurpers had previously ordered the provinces to hunt down and burn Tang law books; whatever escaped the flames no longer retained its original structure.

sentences.zh: 只定州敕庫有本朝法書具在，請敕定州節度使速寫副本進納，庶刑法令式，並合本朝舊制。

translations.literal: Only the edict repository at Ding Prefecture has this dynasty's law books intact; we request an edict to the military governor of Ding Prefecture to speedily copy a duplicate and submit it, so that penal statutes, ordinances, and regulations may all accord with this dynasty's old system.
translations.idiomatic: Only the edict archive at Dingzhou still held a complete Tang set; the memorial asked the emperor to command the Dingzhou governor to copy and forward it at once so statutes, ordinances, and regulations could again match Tang practice.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，定州王都進納唐朝格式律令，凡二百八十六卷。

translations.literal: Before long, Wang Du of Ding Prefecture submitted the Tang formats, statutes, and ordinances, totaling two hundred eighty-six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wang Du of Dingzhou delivered 286 scrolls of Tang formats, statutes, and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 二年二月，刑部尚書盧價奏，纂集《同光刑律統類》凡一十三卷，上之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, Minister of Punishments Lu Jia memorialized, compiled and collected the "Tongguang Comprehensive Categories of Penal Statutes" in thirteen scrolls in all, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 2, Minister of Punishments Lu Jia compiled the thirteen-scroll Tongguang Comprehensive Categories of Penal Statutes and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 周太祖廣順元年六月，敕侍御史盧億、刑部員外郎曹匪躬、大理正段濤同議定重寫法書一百四十八卷。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Guangshun under Zhou Taizu, an edict ordered Attending Censor Lu Yi, Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments Cao Feigong, and Senior Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Duan Tao jointly to deliberate and rewrite the law books in one hundred forty-eight scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Guangshun year 1 (951), Emperor Taizu of Later Zhou ordered attending censor Lu Yi, vice director Cao Feigong in the Ministry of Punishments, and senior reviewing judge Duan Tao to redraft the legal corpus in 148 scrolls.

sentences.zh: 先是，漢隱帝末，因兵亂法書亡失，至是大理奏重寫律令格式、統類編敕，凡改點畫及義理之誤字凡二百一十有四，以晉、漢及國初事關刑法敕條，凡二十六件，分為二卷，附於編敕，目為《大周續編敕》，命省、寺行用焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of Later Han Yin Di, because of military disorder the law books were lost; by now the Court of Judicial Review memorialized rewriting the statutes, ordinances, regulations, formats, comprehensive categories, and compiled edicts—in all two hundred fourteen errors in strokes and in meaning were corrected, and twenty-six edict articles concerning penal law from Jin, Han, and the founding of the state were divided into two scrolls, appended to the compiled edicts, titled "Continued Compiled Edicts of the Great Zhou," and ordered for use by the ministries and courts.
translations.idiomatic: After the law library vanished in the wars at the end of Later Han, the Court of Judicial Review now asked for a full rewrite of statutes, ordinances, regulations, formats, compendia, and compiled edicts. The editors corrected 214 mistaken characters or clauses, gathered twenty-six penal edicts from Jin, Han, and the new Zhou reign into two supplementary scrolls called the Continued Compiled Edicts of the Great Zhou, and put the set into use across the central government.

sentences.zh: （《宋史》：盧億，周初為侍御史，漢末兵亂，法書亡失，至是大理奏重寫律令格式、統類編敕，乃詔億與刑部員外曹匪躬、大理正段濤同加議定舊本，以京兆府改同五府，開封、大名府改同河南府，長安、萬年改為次赤縣，開封、浚儀、大名、元城改為赤縣，又定東京諸門薰風等為京城門，明德等為皇城門，啟運等為宮城門，升龍等為宮門，崇元等為殿門，廟諱書不成字，凡改點畫及義理之誤字二百一十有四。

translations.literal: ("Song History": Lu Yi, at the beginning of Zhou was Attending Censor; at the end of Han because of military disorder the law books were lost; by now the Court of Judicial Review memorialized rewriting the statutes, ordinances, regulations, formats, comprehensive categories, and compiled edicts; then an edict ordered Yi together with Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments Cao Feigong and Senior Judge Duan Tao jointly to deliberate on the old text, changing the Capital Metropolitan Prefecture to rank with the Five Metropolitan Prefectures, Kaifeng and Daming to rank with Henan Metropolitan Prefecture, Chang'an and Wannian to secondary crimson counties, Kaifeng, Junyi, Daming, and Yuancheng to crimson counties, also fixing the eastern capital gates such as Xunfeng as capital-city gates, Mingde as imperial-city gates, Qiyun as palace-city gates, Shenglong as palace gates, Chongyuan as hall gates, taboo characters in writing not forming full graphs—in all two hundred fourteen errors in strokes and in meaning were corrected.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Song History: Lu Yi was an attending censor at the Zhou founding. When Han’s archives burned, the Court of Judicial Review petitioned for a rewrite; Yi, Cao Feigong, and Duan Tao were told to revise the old text—elevating Jingzhao to the rank of the five metropolitan prefectures, aligning Kaifeng and Daming with Henan prefecture, demoting Chang’an and Wannian to “secondary crimson” counties while raising Kaifeng, Junyi, Daming, and Yuancheng to crimson counties, renaming eastern-capital gates (Xunfeng as a capital gate, Mingde as an imperial-city gate, and so on through palace and hall gates), and avoiding taboo graphs that could not be written whole—214 textual and substantive corrections in all.)

sentences.zh: 又以晉、漢及周初事關刑法敕條者，分為二卷，附編敕，目為《大周續編敕》。

translations.literal: Also twenty-six edict articles concerning penal law from Jin, Han, and early Zhou were divided into two scrolls, appended to the compiled edicts, titled "Continued Compiled Edicts of the Great Zhou."
translations.idiomatic: They also sorted twenty-six Jin, Han, and early-Zhou penal edicts into two scrolls appended to the compiled edicts under the title Continued Compiled Edicts of the Great Zhou.

sentences.zh: 詔行之。）〉

translations.literal: An edict ordered implementation.)〉
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the work promulgated.)〉

sentences.zh: 二年二月，中書門下奏：「準元年正月五日赦書節文，今後應犯竊盜贓及和奸者，並依晉天福元年已前條制施行。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year, the Secretariat memorialized: "According to the amnesty text of the fifth day of the first month of the first year, hereafter those who should commit theft of goods by stealth and consensual adultery are all to be handled according to the provisions in force before the first year of Tianfu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 2, the Secretariat cited the amnesty of 5 January in Guangshun year 1: henceforth petty theft and consensual adultery were to be judged under the rules that had applied before Jin’s Tianfu year 1 (936).

sentences.zh: 諸處犯罪人等，除反逆罪外，其餘罪並不籍沒家產、誅及骨肉，一依格令處分者。

translations.literal: Criminals in the various places, apart from crimes of rebellion, for the remaining crimes are not to confiscate family property or execute kin and flesh, all to be disposed according to the regulations and formats.
translations.idiomatic: Except for treason, no offender’s household was to be confiscated and no relatives executed; all other crimes were to follow the code and administrative regulations.

sentences.zh: 請再下明敕，頒示天下。

translations.literal: We request that a clarifying edict again be sent down and promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: They asked that a clarifying edict be reissued empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 」乃下詔曰：「赦書節文，明有厘革，切慮邊城遠郡，未得審詳，宜更申明，免至差誤。

translations.literal: " Then an edict was issued saying: "The amnesty text clearly had revisions; we urgently fear that distant border prefectures and remote commanderies have not obtained full understanding, and it is fitting to clarify again so as to avoid reaching error.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then proclaimed that the amnesty had already reformed several penalties and that remote border districts might not have understood it; the rules needed to be stated again to prevent misapplication.

sentences.zh: 其盜賊，若是強盜，並準自來格條斷遣；

translations.literal: As for robbers, if they are violent robbers, all are to be sentenced and dispatched according to the standing format articles;
translations.idiomatic: Robbery by force would still be sentenced under the longstanding format articles;

sentences.zh: 其犯竊盜者，計贓絹滿三匹已上者，並集眾決殺，其絹以本處上估價為定，不滿三匹者，等第決斷。

translations.literal: those who commit theft by stealth, when the stolen goods in silk valuation reach three bolts or more, are all to be executed before the assembled crowd; the silk is to be fixed by the local upper estimate of value; those not reaching three bolts are to be sentenced by graduated ranks.
translations.idiomatic: petty thieves whose loot was valued at three bolts of silk or more by local price tables were to be executed before the assembled crowd, while lesser amounts drew graduated punishments.

sentences.zh: 應有夫婦人被強奸者，男子決殺，婦人不坐；

translations.literal: Where there are husbands and wives forcibly violated, the man is to be executed by decision, the woman is not punished;
translations.idiomatic: In cases of rape within marriage the assailant was to be put to death and the woman was not punished;

sentences.zh: 其犯和奸者，並準律科斷，罪不至死。

translations.literal: those who commit consensual adultery are all to be sentenced according to the statutes, the crime not reaching death.
translations.idiomatic: consensual adultery was to be judged under the statutes and did not carry the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 其餘奸私罪犯，準格律處分。

translations.literal: The remaining crimes of illicit sexual relations are to be handled according to regulations and formats.
translations.idiomatic: Other sexual offenses would follow the regulations and formats.

sentences.zh: 應諸色罪人，除謀反大逆外，其餘並不得誅殺骨肉、籍沒家產。

translations.literal: Criminals of every category, apart from plotting rebellion and great treason, for the rest are not to execute kin and flesh or confiscate family property.
translations.idiomatic: For all other crimes short of plotting rebellion or great treason, kin were not to be killed and estates were not to be confiscated.

sentences.zh: 」先是，晉天福中敕，凡和奸者，男子婦人並處極法，至是始改從律文焉。

translations.literal: " Earlier, in the Tianfu period of Jin an edict had ordered that for all cases of consensual adultery, men and women alike were to receive the extreme penalty; by now it was first changed to follow the statutory text.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin’s Tianfu edicts consensual adultery had condemned both parties to death; this was the first Zhou measure to restore the statutory standard.

sentences.zh: 世宗顯德四年五月，中書門下奏：「準宣，法書行用多時，文意古質，條目繁細，使人難會，兼前後敕格，互換重疊，亦難詳定。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Xiande under Shizong, the Secretariat memorialized: "According to the proclamation, the law books have been in use for a long time; the text is ancient and plain, the articles numerous and minute, making them hard for people to master, and moreover earlier and later edicts and formats overlap and repeat, also hard to fix with certainty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Xiande year 4 (957), the Secretariat told Emperor Shizong that the penal corpus had grown ancient, minute, and overlapping after long use, so that officials and subjects alike struggled to apply it.

sentences.zh: 宜令中書門下並重刪定，務從節要，所貴天下易為詳究者。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the Secretariat jointly to revise and fix again, striving for brevity and essentials, so that throughout the realm it may be easy to investigate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed a fresh abridgment by the Secretariat that would be concise enough for the empire to study and apply.

sentences.zh: 伏以刑法者御人之銜勒，救弊之斧斤，故鞭撲不可一日弛之於家，刑法不可一日廢之於國，雖堯、舜淳古之代，亦不能舍此而致理矣。

translations.literal: We submit that penal law is the bridle by which one governs people, the axe by which one remedies abuses; therefore flogging cannot for one day be relaxed in the family, and penal law cannot for one day be abandoned in the state—even in the pure antiquity of Yao and Shun one cannot discard this and attain good order.
translations.idiomatic: Penal law, they wrote, was the bridle of governance and the axe of reform: just as the family cannot do without the rod for a single day, the state cannot do without criminal statutes for a single day—even Yao and Shun’s golden age rested on punishment to keep order.

sentences.zh: 今奉制旨刪定律令，有以見聖君欽恤明罰敕法之意也。

translations.literal: Now receiving the imperial order to revise and fix the statutes and ordinances, there is thereby seen the sage ruler's intent of compassionate concern, clear penalties, and admonishing the law.
translations.idiomatic: The commission to revise the statutes showed the emperor’s intent to temper punishments while keeping the law clear.

sentences.zh: 竊以律令之書，政理之本，經聖賢之損益，為古今之章程，歷代以來，謂之彜典。

translations.literal: We submit that books of statutes and ordinances are the root of government and principle; through the sages' additions and subtractions they became the institutions of past and present; generation after generation they have been called the constant canon.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes and ordinances were the foundation of government, refined by the sages into the enduring institutions of every age.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷之所行用者律一十二卷、律疏三十卷、式二十卷、令三十卷、《開成格》一十卷、《大中統類》一十二卷、後唐以來至漢末編敕三十二卷及皇朝制敕等。

translations.literal: What the court now employs are twelve scrolls of statutes, thirty scrolls of statutory commentary, twenty scrolls of regulations, thirty scrolls of ordinances, ten scrolls of "Kaicheng Formats," twelve scrolls of "Comprehensive Categories of the Dazhong Era," thirty-two scrolls of compiled edicts from Later Tang down to the end of Han, and imperial edicts of the present dynasty, and so on.
translations.idiomatic: The working library included twelve scrolls of statutes, thirty of commentary, twenty of regulations, thirty of ordinances, ten Kaicheng formats, twelve Dazhong compendia, thirty-two scrolls of compiled edicts from Later Tang through Later Han, and current imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 折獄定刑，無出於此。

translations.literal: To decide cases and fix penalties, nothing goes outside these.
translations.idiomatic: No trial or sentence was supposed to fall outside this stack of books.

sentences.zh: 律令則文辭古質，看覽者難以詳明；

translations.literal: Statutes and ordinances have ancient and plain wording, and those who look at them find it hard to understand clearly;
translations.idiomatic: The statutes and ordinances were written in archaic prose that readers could barely parse;

sentences.zh: 格敕則條目繁多，檢閱者或有疑誤。

translations.literal: formats and edicts have numerous articles, and those who examine them sometimes have doubts and errors.
translations.idiomatic: the formats and edicts were so numerous that reviewers often stumbled.

sentences.zh: 加之邊遠之地，貪猾之徒，緣此為奸，浸以成弊。

translations.literal: Added to this, in remote border lands greedy and cunning persons take advantage of this to commit wrongdoing, gradually forming abuses.
translations.idiomatic: In distant provinces greedy clerks exploited the confusion, and abuse spread.

sentences.zh: 方屬盛明之運，宜伸畫一之規，所冀民不陷刑，吏知所守。

translations.literal: Now in an age of flourishing clarity, it is fitting to extend the rule of uniform application, hoping that the people will not fall into punishment and officials will know what to uphold.
translations.idiomatic: In an age that called for clarity, they sought one uniform standard so subjects would not fall into punishment and officials would know what to enforce.

sentences.zh: 臣等商量，望準聖旨施行，仍差侍御史知雜事張湜、太子右庶子劇可久、殿中侍御史率汀、職方郎中鄧守中、倉部郎中王瑩、司封員外郎賈比、太常博士趙礪、國子博士李光贊、大理正蘇曉、太子中允王伸等一十人，編集新格，勒成部帙。

translations.literal: Your subjects have deliberated and request implementation according to the sage order, and still to appoint Attending Censor in Charge of Miscellaneous Affairs Zhang Shi, Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household Ju Keyong, Palace Attending Censor Shuai Ting, Bureau Director Deng Shouzhong, Bureau Director Wang Ying, Secretary in the Ministry of Rites Jia Bi, Erudite of the Grand Sacrifices Zhao Li, Erudite of the Directorate of Education Li Guangzan, Senior Judge Su Xiao, and Junior Mentor Wang Shen and nine others in all, to compile a new format and compel completion into fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: They asked to proceed under the imperial command and named a ten-man editorial board—led by Zhang Shi as attending censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, with Ju Keyong, Shuai Ting, Deng Shouzhong, Wang Ying, Jia Bi, Zhao Li, Li Guangzan, Su Xiao, Wang Shen, and others—to compile a new format code in fascicles.

sentences.zh: 律令之有難解者，就文訓釋；

translations.literal: Where statutes and ordinances have passages hard to understand, gloss them according to the text;
translations.idiomatic: Obscure statutory language would be glossed in place;

sentences.zh: 格敕之有繁雜者，隨事刪除。

translations.literal: where formats and edicts are tangled and complex, delete according to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: redundant edicts and formats would be cut to the matter at hand.

sentences.zh: 止要諧理省文，兼且直書易會。

translations.literal: Only require harmonizing principle and reducing text, and moreover direct writing easy to grasp.
translations.idiomatic: The goal was coherent, shortened prose that anyone could follow.

sentences.zh: 其中有輕重未當，便於古而不便於今，矛盾相違，可於此而不可於彼，盡宜改正，無或牽拘。

translations.literal: Among them where severity and lightness are inappropriate, convenient for antiquity but not for the present, contradictory and conflicting, acceptable here but not there—all should be corrected without being constrained.
translations.idiomatic: Any rule that was too harsh, too lenient, suited to antiquity but not to the present, or self-contradictory was to be rewritten without hesitation.

sentences.zh: 候編集畢日，委御史臺、尚書省四品以上及兩省五品以上官參詳可否，送中書門下議定，奏取進止。

translations.literal: When compilation is finished, commission officials of fourth rank and above in the Censorate and Ministry of Revenue and officials of fifth rank and above in the two departments to examine whether it may be used, send to the Secretariat for deliberation and fixing, memorialize and receive decision to proceed or stop.
translations.idiomatic: When the draft was finished, senior censors and ministry officials, together with fifth-rank and above officers of the two secretariats, would review it; the Secretariat would deliberate and memorialists would await the throne’s decision.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 自是湜等於都省集議刪定，仍令大官供膳。

translations.literal: From this Zhang Shi and others assembled at the Department of State Affairs to revise and fix, and still ordered the Court of Imperial Entertainments to supply meals.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi’s team then met at the Department of State Affairs to edit the code, with the Court of Imperial Entertainments ordered to feed them.

sentences.zh: 五年七月，中書門下奏：「侍御史知雜事張湜等九人，奉詔編集刑書，悉有條貫，兵部尚書張昭等一十人，參詳旨要，更加損益。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fifth year, the Secretariat memorialized: "Attending Censor in Charge Zhang Shi and eight others, receiving the edict to compile penal books, all have orderly arrangements; Minister of War Zhang Zhao and nine others, examining the essential points, further added reductions and additions.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 5 the Secretariat reported that Zhang Shi’s nine compilers had produced an orderly draft and that Zhang Zhao’s ten reviewers had refined it further.

sentences.zh: 臣質、臣溥據文評議，備見精審。

translations.literal: Your subjects Zhi and Pu, according to the text deliberating and commenting, fully see it as refined and exact.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Zhi and Pu, reviewing the text, found the work precise and thorough.

sentences.zh: 其所編集者，用律為正；

translations.literal: What they compiled takes the statutes as standard;
translations.idiomatic: The compendium took the statutes as its backbone;

sentences.zh: 辭旨之有難解者，釋以疏意；

translations.literal: where the wording has passages hard to understand, explain with the meaning of the commentary;
translations.idiomatic: where wording was obscure, it borrowed the statutory commentary;

sentences.zh: 義理之有易了者，略其疏文。

translations.literal: where the principle has what is easy to understand, omit the commentary text.
translations.idiomatic: where the sense was plain, commentary was dropped.

sentences.zh: 式令之有附近者次之，格敕之有廢置者又次之。

translations.literal: Among regulations and ordinances, those nearby come next; among formats and edicts, those abolished come after that.
translations.idiomatic: Nearby regulations and ordinances followed next, then obsolete formats and edicts.

sentences.zh: 事有不便於今、該說未盡者，別立新條於本條之下；

translations.literal: Matters inconvenient for the present or whose explanation is not complete have separate new articles placed beneath the original article;
translations.idiomatic: Rules ill suited to the present or incompletely explained received new sub-articles beneath the old ones;

sentences.zh: 其有文理深古、慮人疑惑者，別以朱字訓釋。

translations.literal: those with deep and ancient literary principle, fearing people's doubt and confusion, have separate vermilion-character glosses.
translations.idiomatic: passages so archaic that readers might stumble were glossed in vermilion ink.

sentences.zh: 至於朝廷之禁令，州縣之常科，各以類分，悉令編附。

translations.literal: As for court prohibitions and the standing regulations of prefectures and counties, each is classified by kind and all ordered compiled and attached.
translations.idiomatic: Court bans and standing county regulations were sorted by category and appended.

sentences.zh: 所冀發函展卷，綱目無遺，究本討源，刑政咸在。

translations.literal: What is hoped is that opening the case and unrolling the scroll, the outline has nothing missing; investigating root and seeking source, penal government is all therein.
translations.idiomatic: The editors hoped that opening a single volume would reveal every topic and trace every penalty to its source.

sentences.zh: 其所編集，勒成一部，別有目錄，凡二十一卷。

translations.literal: What they compiled was compelled into one section, separately having a table of contents, twenty-one scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: The finished work comprised twenty-one scrolls with a separate table of contents.

sentences.zh: 刑名之要，盡統於茲，目之為《大周刑統》，欲請頒行天下，與律疏令式通行。

translations.literal: The essentials of penal names are all gathered herein; it is titled "Great Zhou Penal Compendium," and we wish to request promulgation throughout the realm, to circulate together with statutes, commentary, ordinances, and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: It gathered every essential penal category into one book titled the Great Zhou Penal Compendium (Xingtong), which they asked to promulgate empire-wide alongside the statutes, commentary, ordinances, and regulations.

sentences.zh: 其《刑法統類》、《開成格》、編敕等，采掇既盡，不在法司行使之限，自來有宣命指揮公事及三司臨時條法，州縣見今施行，不在編集之數。

translations.literal: The "Comprehensive Categories of Penal Law," "Kaicheng Formats," compiled edicts, and so on, once gathered are exhausted and are not within the limit of what the judicial offices may employ; from past times there have been edict commands directing public business and temporary regulations of the three offices, and what prefectures and counties now implement, not within the number compiled.
translations.idiomatic: Older works such as the Comprehensive Categories of Penal Law, Kaicheng Formats, and compiled edicts had been fully absorbed and would no longer circulate in the judicial offices; ad hoc edicts and three-department rules still in local use were excluded from the compilation.

sentences.zh: 應該京百司公事，逐司各有見行條件，望令本司刪集，送中書門下詳議聞奏。

translations.literal: Public business of the hundred offices in the capital, each office having standing articles now in use, is requested to have that office revise and collect and send to the Secretariat for detailed deliberation and memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Each capital agency was asked to compile its own in-house rules and submit them to the Secretariat for review.

sentences.zh: 」敕宜依，仍頒行天下。

translations.literal: An edict said it was fitting and still to promulgate throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the plan and ordered empire-wide promulgation.

sentences.zh: 乃賜侍御史知雜事張湜等九人各銀器二十兩，雜彩三十匹，賞刪定《刑統》之勞也。

translations.literal: Then Attending Censor in Charge Zhang Shi and nine others were each bestowed twenty taels of silver vessels and thirty bolts of mixed silks, rewarding the labor of revising and fixing the "Penal Compendium."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shi and the other nine chief compilers each received twenty taels of silverware and thirty bolts of patterned silk as reward for completing the Xingtong.

sentences.zh: 唐同光二年六月己巳，敕：「應御史臺河南府行臺馬步司左右軍巡院，見禁囚徒，據罪輕重，限十日內並須決遣申奏。

translations.literal: On the sixth day ji-si of the sixth month of the second year of Tongguang under Tang, an edict: "The Censorate, Henan Prefecture, the mobile secretariat, and the cavalry and infantry offices, left and right military patrol courts—prisoners now detained—according to the lightness or heaviness of the crime, within ten days are all to be decided and dispatched and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: On 6 June in Tongguang year 2 (924), Tang Zhuangzong ordered every prisoner held by the Censorate, Henan prefecture, the mobile secretariat, and the army patrol courts to be sentenced within ten days according to the gravity of the offense and reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 仍委四京、諸道州府，見禁囚徒，速宜疏決，不得淹停，兼恐內外形勢官員私事寄禁，切要止絕，俾無冤滯。

translations.literal: Still commission the four capitals and the prefectures and commanderies of the various circuits—prisoners now detained—to speedily decide and clear, not to detain and delay; also fearing that inside and outside, powerful officials detain people for private affairs, urgently must stop this so there will be no wrongful delay.
translations.idiomatic: All four capitals and provincial prisons were to dispose of cases quickly, without detaining the innocent; officials who jailed people for private grudges were to be stopped so that no one languished unjustly.

sentences.zh: 」三年五月己未，敕：「在京、及諸道州府，所禁罪人，如無大過，速令疏決，不得淹滯。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, day ji-wei, an edict: "In the capital and in the prefectures and commanderies of the various circuits, prisoners detained—if without great fault, speedily order them cleared and decided, not to delay and stagnate."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the following year another edict told capital and provincial jails to release or sentence detainees who had no serious charge without delay.

sentences.zh: 」六月甲寅，敕：「刑以秋冬，雖關惻隱，罪多連累，翻慮滯淹。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, day jia-yin, an edict: "Punishment in autumn and winter, though it concerns compassionate concealment, when crimes mostly involve connected liability, we turn to fear delay and stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: A third edict in the sixth month acknowledged that although executions were traditionally reserved for autumn and winter out of mercy, cases with many co-defendants risked endless detention.

sentences.zh: 若或十人之中，止為一夫抵死，豈可以輕附重，禁錮逾時。

translations.literal: If among ten persons only one man pays with death, how can the light be attached to the heavy and imprisonment exceed the season.
translations.idiomatic: If only one man in ten deserved death, it was wrong to let the light suffer with the heavy and keep everyone shackled past season.

sentences.zh: 言念哀矜，又難全廢。

translations.literal: Speaking of compassionate pity, again it is hard to abolish entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Yet mercy could not be abandoned altogether.

sentences.zh: 其諸司囚徒，罪無輕重，並宜各委本司，據罪詳斷申奏，輕者即時疏理，重者候過立春，至秋分然後行法。

translations.literal: Prisoners of the various offices, crime without lightness or heaviness, all are fitting to have each office according to the crime examine in detail, decide, and memorialize; the light are immediately to be cleared and settled, the heavy wait past the beginning of spring until the autumn equinox and then execute the law.
translations.idiomatic: Every agency was therefore to judge its own prisoners: minor offenders were to be released at once, capital cases were to wait from spring until the autumn equinox before execution.

sentences.zh: 如是事系軍機，須行嚴令，或謀惡逆，或畜奸邪，或行劫殺人，難於留滯，並不在此限。」

translations.literal: If the matter concerns military urgency and strict orders must be carried out, or plotting wicked rebellion, or harboring treacherous evil, or committing robbery and killing people—hard to detain and delay—all are not within this limit."
translations.idiomatic: Military emergencies, treason, sedition, or robbery-homicide were exempt from the seasonal stay.

sentences.zh: 天成元年十一月庚申，敕：「應天下州使系囚，除大辟罪以上，委所在長吏，速推勘決斷，不得傍追證對，經過食宿之地，除當死刑外，並仰釋放，兼不許懲治。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, day geng-shen of the first year of Tiancheng, an edict: "Prisoners detained by prefectural commissioners throughout the realm, apart from capital crimes and above, are entrusted to the local chief officials to speedily investigate, decide, and sentence, not to pursue witnesses on the side; in places passed for lodging and food on the journey, apart from those deserving capital punishment, all are ordered released, and moreover not permitted to punish.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tiancheng year 1 (926), Later Tang ordered that ordinary prisoners outside capital offenses be tried and sentenced by local governors without dragging travelers into collateral interrogations, and that detainees in transit—except those facing death—be released and not mistreated.

sentences.zh: 」二年春。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring,

sentences.zh: 左拾遺李同上言：「天下系囚，請委長吏逐旬親自引問，質其罪狀真虛，然後論之以法，庶無枉濫。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Li Tong submitted: "Prisoners detained throughout the realm—we request entrusting to chief officials personally to question every ten-day period, testing the truth or falsity of the charges, then applying the law to them, hoping there will be no wrongful excess."
translations.idiomatic: left remonstrator Li Tong proposed that every prefectural chief personally review all local prisoners every ten days, verify the charges, and then apply the law so that injustice would not accumulate.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月，大理少卿王郁上言：「凡決極刑，合三覆奏，近年以來，全不守此。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Wang Yu submitted: "Whenever deciding the extreme penalty, it should have three re-memorializations; in recent years this has entirely not been observed.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Vice Director Wang Yu of the Court of Judicial Review noted that capital sentences required three memorial reviews, a rule lately ignored.

sentences.zh: 伏乞今後前一日令各一覆奏。

translations.literal: We submit that hereafter on the day before, each have one re-memorialization.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that henceforth one review be submitted on the day before execution.

sentences.zh: 」奉敕宜依。

translations.literal: Receiving the edict, it was fitting to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The throne assented.

sentences.zh: 八月，西京奏：「奉近敕，在京犯極刑者，令決前一日各一覆奏，緣當府地遠，此後凡有極刑，不審準條疏覆奏。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Western Capital memorialized: "Receiving the recent edict, for those in the capital who commit the extreme penalty, ordering decision one day before each one re-memorialization—because this prefecture is distant, hereafter whenever there is extreme penalty, we do not know whether to follow the article and memorialize for clearance."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Western Capital reported confusion: the new rule required a day-before memorial for executions in Luoyang, but Chang’an was far away and officials were unsure whether they too must memorialize.

sentences.zh: 」奉敕旨：「昨六月二十日所降敕文，只為應在洛京有犯極刑者覆奏，其諸道已降旨命，準舊例施行。

translations.literal: Receiving the edict intent: "The edict text sent down on the twentieth day of the sixth month was only for those in Luoyang who commit the extreme penalty to re-memorialize; the various circuits already had edict orders, following the old precedent in implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The throne clarified that the June 20 edict applied only to capital cases in Luoyang; the provinces should follow their existing precedents.

sentences.zh: 今詳西京所奏，尚未明近敕，兼慮諸道有此疑惑，故令曉諭。

translations.literal: Now examining the Western Capital's memorial, the recent edict is still not clear, and also fearing the various circuits have this doubt; therefore order clarification.
translations.idiomatic: Because Chang’an still seemed uncertain—and other circuits might share the doubt—the court issued a further explanation.

sentences.zh: 」十月辛丑，德音：「為政之要，切在無私；

translations.literal: On the day xin-chou of the tenth month, a virtuous proclamation: "The essential of governing is urgently to be without selfishness;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month an amnesty proclaimed that good government depended on impartiality;

sentences.zh: 聽訟之方，惟期不濫。

translations.literal: the method of hearing litigation is only to hope for no excess.
translations.idiomatic: and fair hearings meant never punishing beyond the charge.

sentences.zh: 天下諸州府官員，如有善推疑獄及曾雪冤濫兼有異政者，當具姓名聞奏，別加甄獎。」

translations.literal: Officials of prefectures and commanderies throughout the realm, if there are those good at resolving doubtful cases or who have once cleared wrongful excess and together have unusual governance, should fully report names and memorialize to the throne, separately to receive selection and reward."
translations.idiomatic: Any prefectural official who resolved hard cases or redressed wrongful convictions was to be named and rewarded.

sentences.zh: 長興元年二月，制曰：「欲通和氣，必在伸冤；

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Changxing, an ordinance said: "Wishing to extend harmonious qi, one must extend wrongful grievances;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Changxing year 1 (930) an ordinance declared that harmony required redressing injustice;

sentences.zh: 將設公方，實資獎善。

translations.literal: wishing to establish public squareness, in truth one relies on rewarding goodness.
translations.idiomatic: and public fairness required rewarding those who did good.

sentences.zh: 州縣官僚能雪冤獄活人生命者，許非時選，仍加階超資註官，與轉服色，已著緋者與轉兼官。

translations.literal: Prefectural and county bureaucrats who can clear wrongful prisons and preserve people's lives are permitted selection out of season, still with added rank and surpassing qualification for office registration, and transfer of robe color; those already wearing crimson receive transfer of concurrent office.
translations.idiomatic: County and prefectural officers who saved lives by overturning wrongful convictions might be promoted off-cycle, gain extra rank, receive higher robe colors, or—if already in crimson—take an additional concurrent post.

sentences.zh: 」二年二月辛亥，敕：「朕猥以眇躬，薦承鴻業，念彼疲瘵，勞於寐興。

translations.literal: On the day xin-hai of the second month of the second year, an edict: "We, mean in this slight body, have ascended to inherit the great enterprise, thinking of those weary and ill, toiling in rising from sleep.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year 2 an edict opened with the emperor’s worry for the afflicted common people who kept him awake at night.

sentences.zh: 或慮官不得人，因成紊亂；

translations.literal: Sometimes we fear officials are not the right men, thereby forming disorder;
translations.idiomatic: He feared that wrong officials bred disorder;

sentences.zh: 或慮刑非其罪，遂至怨嗟。

translations.literal: sometimes we fear punishments do not match crimes, thereby reaching resentment and lament.
translations.idiomatic: and that punishments not matching crimes bred resentment.

sentences.zh: 王化所興，獄訟為本，茍無訓勵，必有滯淹。

translations.literal: What royal transformation raises first is litigation and imprisonment as the root; if there is no instruction and encouragement, there must be delay and stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: Because civilized rule begins in the courts, neglect of prison policy meant inevitable backlog.

sentences.zh: 近日諸道百姓，或諸多違犯，或小可鬥爭。

translations.literal: Recently among the common people of the various circuits, some have many violations, or small quarrels and fights.
translations.idiomatic: Lately some subjects committed serious crimes, others mere brawls.

sentences.zh: 官吏曲縱胥徒，巧求瑕釁。

translations.literal: Officials bend the law to indulge clerks, cleverly seeking flaws.
translations.idiomatic: Yet magistrates indulged their clerks and hunted for pretexts.

sentences.zh: 初則滋張節目，作法拘囚；

translations.literal: At first they then expand sections and items, making methods to detain prisoners;
translations.idiomatic: First they multiplied procedural counts to justify detention;

sentences.zh: 終則誅剝貨財，市恩出拔。

translations.literal: at the end they then extort goods and wealth, buying favor to release and pull out.
translations.idiomatic: then they stripped property and sold release as a favor.

sentences.zh: 外憑公道，內循私情，無理者轉務遷延，有理者卻思退縮。

translations.literal: Outwardly relying on public justice, inwardly following private feeling—those without principle increasingly delay, those with principle then think of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly they spoke of justice while inwardly they followed private whim: the guilty were prolonged, the innocent were driven to withdraw their suits.

sentences.zh: 積成訛弊，漸失紀綱。

translations.literal: Accumulated errors and abuses have gradually caused the loss of statutes and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Errors and abuses piled up over time until statutes and discipline themselves began to slip away.

sentences.zh: 自今後切委逐處官吏州牧縣宰等，深體余懷，各舉爾職。

translations.literal: From now on, earnestly entrust to officials in every locality—prefects, magistrates, and the like—to take deeply to heart my intent and each perform your proper duties.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth I earnestly charge every local official—governors, magistrates, and the rest—to take my intent deeply to heart and each perform the duties proper to your office.

sentences.zh: 凡闕推究，速與剸裁。

translations.literal: Whatever cases lack investigation, swiftly give decisive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever inquiry has been neglected, dispose of the case swiftly and decisively.

sentences.zh: 如敢茍縱依違，遂成枉濫，或經臺訴屈，或投匭申冤，勘問不虛，其元推官典並當責罰，其逐處觀察使、刺史，別議朝典。

translations.literal: If any dare negligently indulge or prevaricate, thereby bringing about wrongful abuse, or if grievances are appealed to the Censorate or petitions of injustice are submitted to the petition box, and upon examination the facts are found true, the original investigating officials and clerks shall all be punished; as for the surveillance commissioners and prefects in each place, their cases shall be separately adjudicated according to court statutes.
translations.idiomatic: If any official dares to indulge wrongdoing or hedge and delay until injustice results—or if a petitioner wins a hearing at the Censorate or lodges a grievance in the petition box and investigation proves the complaint true—the original investigators and clerks shall all be punished, while the surveillance commissioners and prefects in each jurisdiction shall face separate sanctions under court law.

sentences.zh: 宜令諸道州府，各依此處分，所管屬郡，委本道嚴切指揮。

translations.literal: It is appropriate to order each circuit and prefecture to handle matters according to this disposition; for subordinate commanderies under their jurisdiction, each circuit should issue strict directives.
translations.idiomatic: Every circuit and prefecture should act according to this disposition, and each circuit should issue strict orders to the commanderies under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 」八月丁卯，敕：「三京、諸道州府刑獄，近日訪聞，依前禁系人，多不旋決，諸道宜令所在各委長吏，專切推窮，不得有滯淹。」

translations.literal: " In the eighth month, on the day dingmao, an edict: "In the prisons of the three capitals and the prefectures of every circuit, it has recently been learned upon inquiry that, as before, detained persons are in many cases not promptly adjudicated. Every circuit should order the responsible chief official in each place to conduct thorough investigation with dedicated urgency, and allow no delay or detention."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on dingmao, an edict stated: "In the prisons of the three capitals and of prefectures throughout the circuits, recent inquiries show that detainees are still, as before, often left without prompt decision. Each circuit should assign its chief local official to investigate every case with urgent care and permit no backlog or delay."

sentences.zh: 四月，前濮州錄事參軍崔琮上言：「諸道獄囚，恐不依法拷掠，或不勝苦致斃，翻以病聞，請置病囚院，兼加醫藥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Cui Cong, former Registrar of Puzhou, submitted a memorial: "Prisoners in every circuit may fear that torture is not applied according to law, or that they cannot endure the suffering and die, which is then reported as death from illness. I request that sick-prisoner wards be established and that medicine be provided as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Cui Cong, former registrar of Puzhou, memorialized: "Prisoners in the circuits may be tortured unlawfully, or die under torment that is then reported as illness. I ask that sick-prisoner wards be set up and that medical care be provided."

sentences.zh: 」中書覆云：「有罪當刑，仰天無恨；

translations.literal: " The Secretariat replied: "When guilt warrants punishment, one may look to Heaven without resentment;
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat replied: "When guilt deserves punishment, the condemned may face Heaven without resentment;"

sentences.zh: 無病致斃，沒地銜冤。

translations.literal: when death comes without illness, even the earth cannot contain the grievance.
translations.idiomatic: but when a healthy man is tortured to death, his grievance fills the earth itself."

sentences.zh: 燃死灰而必在至仁，照覆盆而須資異鑒。

translations.literal: To stir dead ashes, benevolence must surely be present; to illuminate an overturned basin, extraordinary discernment is required.
translations.idiomatic: To revive what seemed dead ash requires the utmost benevolence; to see justice done in what seemed a covered basin requires extraordinary discernment.

sentences.zh: 《書》著『欽哉』之旨，『《禮》』標『侀也』之文，因彰善於泣辜，更推恩於扇暍。

translations.literal: The Documents records the purport of "Be reverent!"; the Rites marks the text "Pity them!"—thereby showing goodness in weeping for the wrongfully punished, and further extending grace in fanning those scorched by heat.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents sets forth the injunction "Be reverent!"; the Book of Rites marks the phrase "Pity them!"—signs of mercy for the wrongfully punished and of grace extended to those scorched by injustice.

sentences.zh: 所請置病囚院，望依，仍委長吏，專切經心。

translations.literal: As to the request to establish sick-prisoner wards, it is hoped this may be approved; still delegate to the chief official dedicated oversight.
translations.idiomatic: The request to establish sick-prisoner wards is approved; chief officials in each place are to oversee the matter with devoted care.

sentences.zh: 或有病囚，當時遣醫人診候，治療後，據所犯輕重決斷。

translations.literal: Whenever there are sick prisoners, physicians should be sent at once to examine them; after treatment, judgment should be rendered according to the severity of the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a prisoner falls ill, a physician should examine him at once; after treatment, sentence should follow the gravity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 如敢故違，致病囚負屈身亡，本處官吏，並加嚴斷。

translations.literal: If any dare deliberately violate this and cause a sick prisoner to die wrongfully, the local officials shall all receive severe punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If any official deliberately violates this and a sick prisoner dies with his grievance unredressed, every local official involved shall face severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 兼每及夏至，五日一度，差人洗刷枷匣。」

translations.literal: Moreover, at each arrival of the summer solstice, once every five days send men to wash the cangues and fetters."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, at each summer solstice, every five days send men to wash the cangues and fetters."

sentences.zh: 應順元年二月戊午，詔：「應三京、諸道州府系囚，據罪輕重，疾速斷遣。

translations.literal: In the second month of Yingshun, on the day wuwu, an edict: "All detained persons in the three capitals and the prefectures of every circuit should, according to the severity of guilt, be swiftly judged and released.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yingshun, on wuwu, an edict ordered: "Detainees in the three capitals and in prefectures throughout the circuits should, according to the gravity of their offenses, be judged and released without delay."

sentences.zh: 比來停滯，須奏取裁，不便區分，故為留滯。

translations.literal: Recently cases have stagnated because memorials had to be submitted for imperial decision, which was inconvenient for classification; therefore they were held back.
translations.idiomatic: Cases had lately stalled because every decision required a memorial to the throne, which made proper classification awkward and left prisoners waiting.

sentences.zh: 今後凡有刑獄，據理斷遣。

translations.literal: From now on, whenever there are criminal cases, judgment should be rendered according to principle.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whenever a criminal matter arises, judgment should follow the merits of the case.

sentences.zh: 如有敕推按，理合奏聞，不在此限。」

translations.literal: If there is an imperial order to investigate and examine, it is appropriate to memorialize the throne; such cases are not within this limit."
translations.idiomatic: Where the throne orders a special investigation, memorials are still required; those cases lie outside this rule."

sentences.zh: 清泰元年五月丁丑，詔：「在京諸獄及天下州府見系罪人，正當暑毒之時，未免拘囚之苦，誠知負罪，特軫予懷。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Qingtai, on the day dingchou, an edict: "In the prisons of the capital and in prisons throughout the prefectures of the realm, those now detained—at a time when summer heat is at its height—cannot but suffer the pains of imprisonment. I truly know they bear guilt, yet I am especially moved with concern.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Qingtai, on dingchou, an edict said: "In the capital prisons and in prisons across the realm, those now held in custody suffer confinement just as summer heat reaches its height. I know they are guilty, yet my heart is especially moved on their behalf."

sentences.zh: 恐法吏生情，滯於決斷。

translations.literal: I fear that judicial officers may act on personal feeling and delay in judgment.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that judicial officers may indulge private motives and delay judgment.

sentences.zh: 詔至，所在長吏親自慮問，據輕重疾速斷遣，無淹滯。」

translations.literal: When the edict arrives, the chief official in each place should personally examine the cases; according to severity, swiftly judge and release—allow no delay or detention."
translations.idiomatic: When this edict arrives, the chief official in each place should personally review the cases, judge and release according to severity, and permit no backlog or delay."

sentences.zh: 晉天福二年八月，敕下刑部大理寺御史臺及三京、諸道州府：「今後或有系囚染疾者，並令逐處軍醫看候，於公廨錢內量支藥價，或事輕者，仍許家人看候。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of Tianfu of Jin, an edict was sent down to the Ministry of Justice, the Court of Judicial Review, the Censorate, and the three capitals and prefectures of every circuit: "From now on, whenever there are detained persons who contract illness, in every place military physicians should be ordered to attend them; from public-office funds, medicine costs should be allotted as appropriate; or when the matter is minor, family members may still be allowed to attend them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year of Tianfu, an edict went to the Ministry of Justice, the Court of Judicial Review, the Censorate, and the three capitals and every circuit: "Whenever a detainee falls ill, local military physicians should attend him, medicine paid from public-office funds as appropriate; in lighter cases, family members may still attend."

sentences.zh: 」四年九月，相州節度使桑維翰奏：「管內所獲賊人，從來籍沒財產，雲是鄴都舊例，格律未見明文。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month of the fourth year, Sang Weihan, military commissioner of Xiangzhou, memorialized: "Bandits captured within my jurisdiction have always had their property confiscated—said to follow an old precedent of the Ye capital—but the statutes contain no explicit provision.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year, Sang Weihan, commissioner of Xiangzhou, memorialized: "Bandits taken in my jurisdiction have always had their property confiscated—said to follow an old Ye capital practice—but the code contains no explicit rule for this."

sentences.zh: 」敕：「今後凡有賊人，準格定罪，不得沒納家資。

translations.literal: " An edict: "From now on, whenever there are bandits, sentence according to the code; do not confiscate family assets.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Henceforth, whenever bandits are captured, sentence them under the code and do not confiscate their families' property."

sentences.zh: 天下諸州，準此處分。

translations.literal: All prefectures throughout the realm should handle matters according to this disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture in the realm should follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 」三月庚午，詳定院奏：「前守洪洞縣主簿盧燦進策云：『伏以刑獄至重，朝廷所難，尚書省分職六司，天下謂之會府，且諸道決獄，若關人命，即刑部不合不知。

translations.literal: " On the day gengwu of the third month, the Commission for Detailed Review memorialized: "The former Principal Recorder of Hongtong County, Lu Can, submitted a policy proposal, saying: 'I humbly consider that criminal cases are of the utmost gravity and are what the court finds most difficult; the Department of State Affairs divides duties among six ministries and is called the chief office of the realm—and when circuits render judgment in cases touching human life, the Ministry of Justice ought not to be kept uninformed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu of the third month, the Commission for Detailed Review memorialized: "Lu Can, former principal recorder of Hongtong County, proposed: 'Criminal cases are supremely grave and among the hardest matters for the court; the Department of State Affairs divides the six ministries and is the realm's chief office—yet when a circuit decides a capital case, the Ministry of Justice should not be left uninformed.'"

sentences.zh: 欲請州府凡斷大辟罪人訖，逐季具有無申報刑部，仍俱錄案款事節，並本判官、馬步都虞候、司法參軍、法直官、馬步司判官名銜申聞，所貴或有案內情曲不圓，刑部可行覆勘。

translations.literal: I request that whenever prefectures have finished judging persons subject to the death penalty, each quarter they should fully report whether or not they have notified the Ministry of Justice, and should also submit together the case record, circumstances, and the names and titles of the presiding judge, the infantry and cavalry chief inspectors, the judicial aide, the legal reviewer, and the infantry and cavalry division judges, so that if any aspect of the case is not fully rounded, the Ministry of Justice may conduct a review.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that whenever a prefecture completes a capital sentence, each quarter it report to the Ministry of Justice and submit the full case record, circumstances, and the names and titles of the presiding judge, the infantry and cavalry inspectors, the judicial aide, the legal reviewer, and the division judges, so that if any point in the case remains incomplete, the ministry may review it.

sentences.zh: 如此則天下遵守法律，不敢輕易刑書，非惟免有銜冤，抑亦勸其立政者。

translations.literal: In this way the realm will observe the laws and not lightly treat the penal code—not only sparing the wrongfully aggrieved, but also encouraging those who establish good government.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the realm would honor the law and not treat the penal code lightly—sparing the wronged and encouraging sound governance alike.

sentences.zh: 』臣等參詳，伏以人命至重，國法須精，雖載舊章，更宜條理，誠為允當，望賜施行。

translations.literal: ' Your subjects have examined this in detail and humbly consider that human life is of the utmost gravity and state law must be precise; although the old statutes are recorded, they should further be set in order; this is truly appropriate and we hope it may be granted implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorialists reviewed the proposal and observed that human life is supremely grave and state law must be exact; though the old statutes record the principle, they should be set in clearer order. The proposal was deemed fitting and recommended for enactment.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " Approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔曰：「刑獄之難，古今所重，但關人命，實動天心，或有冤魂，則傷和氣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict said: "The difficulty of criminal prisons is what ancients and moderns alike have regarded as weighty; whenever human life is involved, it truly stirs the heart of Heaven; if wronged spirits remain, then harmonious qi is harmed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, an edict declared: "The difficulty of prisons is a burden ancients and moderns alike have taken seriously; whenever a human life is at stake, Heaven's heart is truly moved; lingering wronged spirits injure the realm's harmonious qi."

sentences.zh: 應諸道州府，凡有囚徒，據推勘到案款，一一盡理，子細檢律令格敕。

translations.literal: In every circuit and prefecture, whenever there are prisoners, according to the results of investigation, examine every item of the case record with care and scrutinize the statutes, regulations, and edicts.
translations.idiomatic: In every circuit and prefecture, for every prisoner, once investigation is complete, examine each point of the record carefully against the statutes, regulations, and edicts.

sentences.zh: 其間或有疑者，準令文讞，大理寺亦疑，申尚書省，省寺明有指歸，州府然後決遣。」

translations.literal: If in the midst of these there are doubtful points, follow the statutory interpretation; if the Court of Judicial Review is also in doubt, memorialize the Department of State Affairs; when the department and court have clear direction, the prefecture may then render judgment and release."
translations.idiomatic: Where doubt remains, follow statutory interpretation; if the Court of Judicial Review is still uncertain, memorialize the Department of State Affairs; only when department and court give clear direction may the prefecture judge and dispose of the case."

sentences.zh: 五年三月丙子，詔曰：「自大中六年已來，嫠耳稱冤，決杖流配，訴雖有理，不在申明。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year, on the day bingzi, an edict said: "Since the sixth year of Dazhong, widows who cut their ears to proclaim injustice have still been flogged and exiled—even when their appeals had merit, they were not allowed to state their case.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year, on bingzi, an edict stated: "Since the sixth year of Dazhong, widows who mutilated their ears to proclaim injustice were still flogged and exiled—even when their grievance was justified, they were denied a hearing."

sentences.zh: 今後據其所陳，與為勘斷，剺耳之罪，準律別科。

translations.literal: From now on, according to what they state, investigate and judge for them; the crime of ear-cutting should be separately sentenced according to the code.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, investigate and judge according to what they allege; the offense of ear-cutting should be sentenced separately under the code."

sentences.zh: 」六年秋七月庚辰，詔曰：「政教所切，獄訟惟先，推窮須察於事情，斷遣必遵於條法，用宏欽恤，以致和平。

translations.literal: " In the seventh month of autumn of the sixth year, on the day gengchen, an edict said: "Among the concerns of government and instruction, litigation comes first; investigation must discern the circumstances of the matter, and judgment and release must follow the articles of law—thereby extending compassionate concern and achieving peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year, on gengchen, an edict said: "Among the duties of government, litigation comes first: investigation must probe the facts, and judgment must obey the code—thereby extending compassionate care and securing peace."

sentences.zh: 應三京、鄴都及諸道州府，見禁諸色人等，宜令逐處長吏，常切提撕，疾速決遣，每務公當，勿使滯淹。

translations.literal: In the three capitals, the Ye capital, and the prefectures of every circuit, all persons now detained of every category should be urged by the chief official in each place with constant vigilance; swiftly judge and release, in every matter seek fairness, and do not allow delay or detention.
translations.idiomatic: In the three capitals, Ye, and every circuit prefecture, the chief official in each place should keep constant watch over all detainees, judge and release them swiftly, seek fairness in every case, and permit no backlog.

sentences.zh: 」天福八年四月壬申，敕：「朕自臨寰宇，思致和平，思將以四海為家，慮有一物失所。

translations.literal: " In the fourth month of the eighth year of Tianfu, on the day renshen, an edict: "Since I took the realm, I have thought to bring peace; I think to make the four seas one household, yet I fear that even one thing may lose its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the eighth year of Tianfu, on renshen, an edict read: "Since I assumed the realm I have sought peace; I would make the four seas one household, yet I fear that even one creature may be wronged."

sentences.zh: 每念狴牢之內，或多枉撓之人，屬此炎蒸，倍宜軫憫，冀絕滯淹之嘆，用資欽恤之仁。

translations.literal: Whenever I think of those within the prisons, many are persons wrongfully oppressed; at this season of blazing heat, compassion is doubly fitting, hoping to end the sighs of delay and detention and thereby supply the benevolence of compassionate concern.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever I think of those in prison, many are wrongfully oppressed; in this season of blazing heat compassion is doubly due, that the sighs of delay may cease and the throne's merciful care be made real.

sentences.zh: 應三京、鄴都及諸道州府見禁罪人等，宜令逐處長吏，嚴切指揮本推司及委本所判官，疾速結絕斷遣，不得淹延，及致冤濫，仍付所司。」

translations.literal: All persons now detained for crime in the three capitals, the Ye capital, and the prefectures of every circuit should be ordered by the chief official in each place, with strict directives to the investigating office and to the assigned judge in each office, to conclude and judge and release swiftly, without delay, and without causing wrongful abuse; still transmit this to the responsible offices."
translations.idiomatic: All detainees in the three capitals, Ye, and every circuit should be ordered by local chief officials, with strict instructions to investigating offices and assigned judges, to conclude cases swiftly, without delay or wrongful abuse; the responsible offices are charged accordingly."

sentences.zh: 開運二年五月壬戌，殿中丞桑簡能上封事曰：「伏以天地育萬物，廣博厚之恩；

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Kaiyun, on the day renxu, Palace Director Sang Jianneng submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "I humbly consider that Heaven and Earth nurture the ten thousand things with broad, deep, and generous favor;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year of Kaiyun, on renxu, Palace Director Sang Jianneng submitted a sealed memorial: "Heaven and Earth nurture the ten thousand things with vast and generous favor;"

sentences.zh: 帝王牧黎元，行寬大之令。

translations.literal: emperors shepherd the black-haired people and enact orders of leniency and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: emperors shepherd the common people and issue orders of leniency and breadth."

sentences.zh: 是知恤刑緩獄，乃為政之先；

translations.literal: Thus one knows that compassionate concern for punishment and easing of prisons is foremost in governance;
translations.idiomatic: Thus compassionate punishment and eased prisons are the first duties of governance;

sentences.zh: 布德行惠，實愛民之本。

translations.literal: to spread virtue and enact grace is truly the root of loving the people.
translations.idiomatic: and to spread virtue and enact grace is truly the root of cherishing the people.

sentences.zh: 今盛夏之月，農事方殷，是雷風長養之時，乃動植蕃蕪之際。

translations.literal: Now in the month of full summer, agricultural affairs are at their height; this is the season when thunder and wind nurture growth, the time when moving and rooted things flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Now, at the height of summer, farming presses at its peak—the season when thunder and wind nurture growth, when every living thing flourishes.

sentences.zh: 宜順時令，以宏至仁。

translations.literal: One should follow the season and thereby extend the utmost benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The season itself calls for the utmost benevolence.

sentences.zh: 竊以諸道州府都郡縣應見禁罪人，或有久在囹圄，稍滯區分，胥吏侮文，枝蔓乃眾。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that in the chief prefectures, commanderies, and counties of every circuit, among prisoners now detained, some have long been in prison and their cases slightly delayed in classification; clerks despise the documents and the branching complications are many.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that in the chief prefectures, commanderies, and counties of every circuit, among prisoners now held, some have languished long in jail while their cases stall; clerks trifle with the paperwork until the tangle of delays grows thick.

sentences.zh: 捶楚之下。

translations.literal: Beneath the rod and whip.
translations.idiomatic: Beneath rod and whip,

sentences.zh: 或陷無辜；

translations.literal: some are trapped though innocent;
translations.idiomatic: some innocent men are trapped;

sentences.zh: 縲紲之中，莫能自理。

translations.literal: within bonds, none can plead their own case.
translations.idiomatic: within fetters, none can plead his own cause.

sentences.zh: 茍一人拘系，則數人營財，物用既殫，工業亦罷。

translations.literal: If one person is detained, then several persons must raise funds; goods and supplies are exhausted and crafts and trades also cease.
translations.idiomatic: When one man is detained, several must raise funds for him; household goods are spent and trades and crafts come to a halt.

sentences.zh: 若此之類，實繁有徒，切恐官吏因循，浸成斯弊。

translations.literal: Cases of this kind are truly numerous; I urgently fear that officials may follow precedent and gradually bring this abuse to completion.
translations.idiomatic: Such cases are legion, and I fear that if officials follow routine, this abuse will only deepen.

sentences.zh: 伏乞降詔旨，令所在刑獄，委長吏親自錄問，量罪疾速斷遣，務絕冤濫，勿得淹留，庶免虛禁平人，妨奪農力，冀召和氣，以慶明時。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that an edict be sent down, ordering the prisons in every place to have the chief official personally record and examine cases, judge and release according to guilt with speed, strive to end wrongful abuse, and not detain; thereby sparing the false imprisonment of common people, avoiding the hindrance of agricultural labor, and hoping to summon harmonious qi to celebrate this enlightened age.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that an edict order prisons everywhere to have the chief official personally examine cases, judge and release according to guilt without delay, end wrongful abuse, and forbid detention—sparing common people false imprisonment, preserving farm labor, and summoning harmonious qi to bless this enlightened age."

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「囹圄之中，縲紲之苦，奸吏茍窮於枝蔓，平人用費於貨財，由茲滯淹，兼致屈塞。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "Within the prison, the suffering of fetters; corrupt clerks may exhaust the branching complications, and common people spend their goods and wealth—thereby causing delay and detention, and also bringing about obstruction and injustice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "In prison, fetters bring suffering; corrupt clerks spin out endless complications while common people spend their wealth—delay piles up and injustice is blocked."

sentences.zh: 桑簡能體茲軫憫，專有敷陳，請長吏躬親，免獄官抑逼，深為允當，宜再頌行。

translations.literal: Sang Jianneng took this compassionate concern to heart and set forth a dedicated proposal, requesting that chief officials act in person and spare prisoners from the pressure of jail officers; this is deeply appropriate and should again be proclaimed and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Jianneng voiced this compassionate concern in a focused proposal, asking that chief officials act in person and spare prisoners from jailers' pressure; the court found this deeply fitting and ordered it proclaimed again."

sentences.zh: 宜依。

translations.literal: It is appropriate to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Approved as proposed.

sentences.zh: 」十月甲子，秘書省著作郎邊玕上封事曰：「臣聞從諫如流，人君之令範；

translations.literal: " On the day jiazi of the tenth month, Bian Gan, Archivist of the Secretariat, submitted a sealed memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that accepting remonstrance like a flowing stream is the ruler's model;
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi of the tenth month, Bian Gan, archivist of the Secretariat, submitted a sealed memorial: "I have heard that accepting remonstrance like a flowing stream is a ruler's model;"

sentences.zh: 極言無隱，臣子之常規。

translations.literal: to speak to the utmost without concealment is the minister's constant rule.
translations.idiomatic: and to speak plainly without concealment is a minister's constant duty."

sentences.zh: 蓋欲表大國之任人，致萬邦之無事，前文備載，可舉而行。

translations.literal: This is because one wishes to show that a great state employs men and thereby brings the ten thousand regions to peace; the former text fully records this and may be raised up and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: This is how a great state shows that it employs men rightly and brings the myriad realms to peace; the ancients recorded it fully, and we may act on it now.

sentences.zh: 伏以皇帝陛下，德合上玄，運膺下武，旰食宵衣而軫念，好生惡殺以推仁，幾措典刑，固無冤枉。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty, the Emperor, virtue joins with the Supreme Ultimate and the mandate accords with martial excellence below; with meals taken at dawn and garments changed at night, you are moved with concern; loving life and hating killing, you extend benevolence—almost placing canonical punishments in abeyance, so that in truth there are no wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's virtue joins with Heaven and your mandate answers the age; you rise at dawn and sleep late with care, loving life and hating killing, extending benevolence until canonical punishments nearly fall still and, in truth, injustice is rare.

sentences.zh: 然以照臨之內，州郡尤多，若不再具舉明，伏恐漸成奸弊。

translations.literal: Yet within the realm of your illumination, prefectures and commanderies are especially many; if this is not again fully set forth and made clear, I humbly fear that gradually corrupt practices will take shape.
translations.idiomatic: Yet within your illuminated realm prefectures and commanderies are countless; unless this is proclaimed again in full detail, corrupt practice may gradually return.

sentences.zh: 臣竊見諸道刑獄，前朝曾降敕文，凡是禁系罪人，五日一度錄問。

translations.literal: Your subject has observed that in the prisons of every circuit, in former dynasties edicts were sent down: for all detained persons, once every five days there should be recording and examination.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that in former dynasties edicts ordered that in every circuit's prisons, every detained person should be examined and recorded once every five days.

sentences.zh: 但以年月稍遠，漸致因循。

translations.literal: But because the years have grown somewhat distant, gradually this has fallen into routine neglect.
translations.idiomatic: But as years passed, the rule slipped into neglect.

sentences.zh: 或長吏事煩，不暇躬親點檢；

translations.literal: Or the chief official may be burdened with affairs and have no leisure personally to inspect;
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes the chief official is overwhelmed and cannot inspect in person;

sentences.zh: 或胥徒啟幸，妄要追領證明。

translations.literal: or clerks and runners may seek favor and falsely demand the pursuit and production of proof.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes clerks and runners seek advantage and falsely demand witnesses and documents.

sentences.zh: 慮有涉於淫刑，即恐傷於和氣。

translations.literal: If there is involvement in excessive punishment, then I fear that harmonious qi will be harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Where excessive punishment follows, harmonious qi is harmed.

sentences.zh: 伏乞特降詔敕。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that a special edict be sent down.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that a special edict be issued.

sentences.zh: 自今後諸道並委長吏五日一度，當面同共錄問，所冀處法者無恨，銜冤者獲伸。

translations.literal: From now on, in every circuit entrust to the chief official, once every five days, to conduct recording and examination together face to face, so that those punished by law may be without resentment and those bearing grievances may obtain redress.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, in every circuit the chief official should every five days examine detainees face to face, so that the punished may feel no resentment and the aggrieved may obtain redress.

sentences.zh: 俾令四海九州，鹹歌聖德；

translations.literal: Thus cause the four seas and nine regions all to sing of sagely virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Then the four seas and nine regions may sing of sagely virtue;

sentences.zh: 五風十雨，永致昌期。

translations.literal: with the five winds and ten rains, forever reach an age of prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: and with timely winds and rains, reach an age of lasting prosperity."

sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「人之命無以復生，國之刑不可濫舉。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "A person's life, once lost, cannot be restored; the state's punishments cannot be lightly applied.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "A human life, once taken, cannot be restored; the state's punishments must not be lightly applied."

sentences.zh: 雖一成之典，務在公平；

translations.literal: Although the statutes once fixed require fairness in execution;
translations.idiomatic: Though the code once fixed demands fairness in execution,

sentences.zh: 而三覆其詞，所宜詳審。

translations.literal: yet thrice to review the words is what should be examined in detail.
translations.idiomatic: threefold review of the words is what should be examined in detail.

sentences.zh: 凡居法吏，合究獄情。

translations.literal: All who hold office in the law should thoroughly investigate prison circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Every judicial officer should thoroughly investigate the circumstances of each prison case.

sentences.zh: 邊玕近陟周行，俄陳讜議，更彰欽恤，宜允申明。」

translations.literal: Bian Gan has recently been promoted in the court ranks and soon offered forthright counsel, further displaying compassionate concern; it is appropriate to grant approval and proclaim this."
translations.idiomatic: Bian Gan has lately risen in court rank and promptly offered forthright counsel, further displaying the throne's merciful care; approval and proclamation are granted."

sentences.zh: 三年十一月丁未，左拾遺竇儼上疏曰：「臣伏睹名例律疏云：死刑者，古先哲王，則天垂象，本欲生之，義期止殺，絞斬之坐，皆刑之極也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year, on the day dingwei, Left Remonstrator Dou Yan submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has observed that the commentary to the Statutes on Names states: 'For the death penalty, the ancient sage kings, in accordance with Heaven, set forth symbols—the original intent was to give life, the meaning was to stop killing; the punishments of strangulation and decapitation are all at the extreme of penalties.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the third year, on dingwei, Left Remonstrator Dou Yan memorialized: "The commentary to the Statutes on Names states: 'For the death penalty, the ancient sage kings, following Heaven's signs, meant to preserve life and to halt killing; strangulation and decapitation stand at the extreme of punishment.'"

sentences.zh: 又準天成三年閏八月二十三日敕，行極法日，宜不舉樂，減常膳；

translations.literal: Moreover, according to the edict of the twenty-third day of the intercalary eighth month of the third year of Tiancheng, on days when the extreme penalty is carried out, music should not be performed and the regular meal should be reduced;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, by the edict of the intercalary eighth month, twenty-third day, of the third year of Tiancheng, on days when capital punishment is carried out, music should cease and the regular meal be reduced;

sentences.zh: 又刑部式，決重杖一頓處死，以代極法，斯皆人君哀矜不舍之道也。

translations.literal: and in the formulary of the Ministry of Justice, where heavy beating in one session replaces death in place of the extreme penalty—all these are the way of the ruler's compassionate concern and unwillingness to abandon.
translations.idiomatic: and in the Ministry of Justice formulary, where a single heavy beating replaces execution—all these embody the ruler's compassionate reluctance to abandon life.

sentences.zh: 竊以蚩尤為五虐之科，尚行鞭樸；

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Chiyou established the five cruel punishments, yet still applied the whip;
translations.idiomatic: Chiyou devised the five cruel punishments, yet still used the whip;

sentences.zh: 漢祖約三章之法，止有死刑。

translations.literal: the Han founder agreed on the law in three chapters, and there was only the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: the Han founder's three-chapter law recognized only death.

sentences.zh: 絞者筋骨相連，斬者頭頸異處，大辟之目，不出兩端，淫刑所興，近聞數等。

translations.literal: Strangulation leaves sinew and bone connected; decapitation separates head and neck—the categories of great execution do not go beyond these two ends; excessive punishments have lately been heard in several grades.
translations.idiomatic: Strangulation leaves flesh and bone joined; decapitation severs head from neck—the great executions know only these two forms, yet lately several grades of excessive punishment have been heard.

sentences.zh: 蓋緣外地，不守通規，肆率情性，或以長釘貫篸人手足，或以短刀臠割人肌膚，乃至累朝半生半死，俾冤聲而上達，致和氣以有傷。

translations.literal: This is because in outer regions they do not keep to the universal regulations but freely follow personal inclination—sometimes using long nails to pierce through a person's hands and feet, or short knives to slice a person's flesh and skin, even to several reigns of half living and half dead, causing cries of injustice to reach above and harming harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Outer regions ignore the universal code and follow private whim—driving long nails through hands and feet, slicing flesh with short knives, leaving men half alive for reign after reign until cries of injustice reach Heaven and harmonious qi is wounded.

sentences.zh: 將宏守位之仁，在峻惟行之令，欲乞特下明敕，嚴加禁斷者。

translations.literal: To extend the benevolence of guarding one's position, and to make strict the order of careful execution, I wish to beg that a clear edict be specially sent down and strictly forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: To extend the benevolence proper to the throne and to make execution strict and lawful, I beg that a clear edict forbid and cut off such practices."
