sentences.zh: 」敕曰：「文物方興，刑罰須當，有罪宜從於正法，去邪漸契於古風。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "As culture and institutions are rising, punishments must be fitting; the guilty should follow the proper law, and removing evil should gradually accord with ancient custom.
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "As culture and institutions rise, punishments must be fitting; the guilty should face proper law, and the purging of evil should return toward ancient custom."

sentences.zh: 竇儼所貢奏章，實裨理道，宜依所奏，準律令施行。」

translations.literal: The memorial chapter submitted by Dou Yan truly assists the principles of governance; it is appropriate to follow what was memorialized and implement according to the statutes and regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Dou Yan's memorial truly serves good governance; it is ordered implemented according to the statutes and regulations."

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐二年正月，敕：「政貴寬易，刑尚哀矜，慮滋蔓之生奸，實軫傷而是念。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Qianyou of Han, an edict: "In government, breadth and ease are prized; in punishments, compassionate concern is honored—fearing that spreading abuses will breed wickedness, yet truly moved with concern for injury.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Qianyou, an edict declared: "Government prizes breadth and ease; punishments honor compassionate care—fearing that spreading abuse breeds wickedness, yet truly moved by every injury."

sentences.zh: 今屬三元改候，四序履端，將冀和平，無如獄訟。

translations.literal: Now at the change of the three origins and the turn of the four seasons at year's beginning, I will hope for peace—nothing is like litigation.
translations.idiomatic: Now, as the three origins turn and the year's four seasons begin anew, I look for peace—and nothing stands more in the way than litigation.

sentences.zh: 應三京、鄴都、諸道州府見系罪人，委逐處長吏躬親慮問，其於決斷，務在公平，但見其情，即為具獄，勿令率引，遂致淹停，無縱舞文，有傷和氣。

translations.literal: All prisoners now detained in the three capitals, the Ye capital, and the prefectures of every circuit should be entrusted to the chief official in each place to examine personally; in judgment, strive for fairness—whenever the circumstances are seen, complete the case record at once; do not allow leading questions to cause delay and stoppage; do not indulge distortion of the text and thereby harm harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: All detainees in the three capitals, Ye, and every circuit should be examined by local chief officials in person; judgment must be fair—when the facts are clear, complete the record at once; do not prolong cases with leading questions or distort the law to harm harmonious qi."

sentences.zh: 」四月甲午，敕曰：「月戒正陽，候當小暑，乃挺重出輕之日，是恤刑議獄之辰，有罪者速就勘窮，薄罰者畫時疏決，用符時令，勿縱滯淹。

translations.literal: " On the day jiawu of the fourth month, an edict said: "The monthly warning is the proper yang; the season should be minor heat—this is the day for drawing forth the heavy and bringing forth the light, the time for compassionate concern for punishment and deliberation on prisons; those with guilt should swiftly undergo thorough investigation, and those with light penalties should at once be judged and released, thereby accord with the season and not indulge delay or detention.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu of the fourth month, an edict said: "The monthly warning marks proper yang and minor heat approaches—the day for easing the severe and releasing the light, the season for merciful punishment and prison deliberation; the guilty should be swiftly investigated, the lightly punished promptly released, in accord with the season and without delay."

sentences.zh: 三京、鄴都、諸道州府在獄見系罪人，宜令所司疾速斷遣，無致淹滯枉濫。

translations.literal: Prisoners now detained in the prisons of the three capitals, the Ye capital, and the prefectures of every circuit should be ordered by the responsible offices to judge and release swiftly, without causing delay, detention, or wrongful abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Detainees in the three capitals, Ye, and every circuit should be judged and released swiftly by the responsible offices, without delay, detention, or wrongful abuse."

sentences.zh: 」五月辛未，敕：「政化所先，獄訟攸切，不惟枉撓，兼慮滯淹。

translations.literal: " In the fifth month, on the day xinwei, an edict: "Among what government and transformation put first, litigation is urgent—not only wrongful oppression, but also delay and detention.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on xinwei, an edict stated: "Among the first duties of government, litigation is urgent—not only wrongful oppression but delay and detention as well."

sentences.zh: 適當長養之時，正屬熇蒸之候，累行條貫，俾速施行，靡不丁寧，未曾奏報，再頌告諭，無或因循。

translations.literal: This suits the season of nurturing growth and falls in the season of blazing heat; regulations have repeatedly been issued to secure swift implementation—none have failed to be urged in detail, yet none have been memorialized in report; again proclaim and instruct, and let there be no following precedent.
translations.idiomatic: This is the season of growth and blazing heat; edicts have been issued again and again for swift execution, urged in every detail, yet never reported back; proclaim them once more and permit no further neglect."

sentences.zh: 應三京、鄴都、諸道州府，詔至，宜具疏放已行未行申奏，無致逗留」

translations.literal: In the three capitals, the Ye capital, and the prefectures of every circuit, when the edict arrives, each should fully memorialize what releases have been carried out and what have not, and memorialize—do not cause delay."
translations.idiomatic: In the three capitals, Ye, and every circuit, when the edict arrives each region should memorialize in full which releases have been carried out and which have not—permit no delay."

sentences.zh: 周廣順三年四月乙亥，敕：「朕以時當化育，氣屬炎蒸，乃思縲紲之人，是軫哀矜之念，慮其非所，案鞫淹延，或枉濫窮屈而未得申宣，或饑渴疾病而無所控告。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Guangshun of Zhou, on the day yihai, an edict: "I, at a time when transformation and nurturing hold sway and the qi belongs to blazing heat, think of those in fetters and am moved with the thought of compassionate concern—fearing that they are not where they should be, that examination and judgment are delayed, or that wrongful abuse and extreme oppression obtain no channel for appeal, or that hunger, thirst, and illness find no means of complaint.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Guangshun, on yihai, an edict read: "At a time of nurturing transformation and blazing heat, I think of those in fetters with compassionate care—fearing that investigation drags on, that the wrongfully oppressed cannot appeal, or that hunger, thirst, and sickness find no voice."

sentences.zh: 以罪當刑者，惟彼自召，法不可移；

translations.literal: Those whose crime warrants punishment have only themselves to summon it; the law cannot be moved;
translations.idiomatic: Those whose crime warrants punishment have summoned it themselves; the law cannot be bent;

sentences.zh: 非理受苦者，為上不明，安得無慮。

translations.literal: those who suffer without reason do so because those above are not clear—how can there be no concern?
translations.idiomatic: but those who suffer without reason do so because authority above is unclear—how can I not be concerned?

sentences.zh: 欽恤之道，夙宵靡寧。

translations.literal: The way of compassionate concern—morning and night, there is no peace.
translations.idiomatic: The way of merciful care leaves me restless morning and night.

sentences.zh: 應諸道州府見系罪人，宜令官吏疾速推鞫，據輕斷遣，不得淹滯。

translations.literal: All prisoners now detained in the prefectures of every circuit should be ordered by officials to investigate swiftly and, according to severity, judge and release, without delay or detention.
translations.idiomatic: All detainees in every circuit should be swiftly investigated by officials, judged and released according to severity, without delay.

sentences.zh: 仍令獄吏，灑掃牢獄，當令虛歇；

translations.literal: Still order the prison officers to sprinkle and sweep the prisons, so that they should be kept vacant when possible;
translations.idiomatic: Prison officers are also ordered to sweep the prisons clean and keep cells empty whenever possible;

sentences.zh: 洗滌枷械，無令蚤虱；

translations.literal: Wash the cangues and restraints; do not allow lice and fleas;
translations.idiomatic: wash cangues and restraints so lice and fleas do not infest them;

sentences.zh: 供給水漿，無令饑渴。

translations.literal: supply water and gruel; do not allow hunger and thirst.
translations.idiomatic: provide water and thin gruel so prisoners do not hunger or thirst.

sentences.zh: 如有疾患，令其家人看承，囚人無主，官差醫工診候，勿致病亡。

translations.literal: If there is illness, have their families attend them; for prisoners without kin, the government should dispatch medical officers to examine and treat them—do not allow death from disease.
translations.idiomatic: When a prisoner falls ill, let his family nurse him; if he has no family, assign a government physician to treat him and prevent death from sickness.

sentences.zh: 循典法之成規，順長嬴之時令，俾無淹滯，以致治平。

translations.literal: Follow the established rules of canonical law, accord with the seasonal ordinance of the season of flourishing growth, so that there is no delay or detention, and governance reaches tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: Follow established legal procedure, observe the season of growth, clear every backlog, and bring about good order."

sentences.zh: 」又，賜諸州詔曰：「朕以敷政之勤，惟刑是重，既未能化人於無罪，則不可為上而失刑。

translations.literal: " Further, an edict granted to the various prefectures said: "I, with diligence in spreading governance, regard punishment alone as weighty; since I have not yet been able to transform people so that none are guilty, I cannot as sovereign neglect punishment.
translations.idiomatic: A separate edict to every prefecture read: "In governing diligently I hold punishment in the gravest regard; having not yet taught all men to live without crime, a ruler cannot afford to let the law lapse.

sentences.zh: 況時當長嬴，事貴清適，念囹圄之閉固，復桎梏之拘縻，處於炎蒸，何異焚灼。

translations.literal: Moreover, the season is now the flourishing phase; affairs value clarity and ease; pondering the closed solidity of the prisons and again the binding restraint of fetters and cangues—to be in scorching heat is no different from burning.
translations.idiomatic: Now the season of flourishing growth calls for clarity and ease. Men shut in prisons, bound in fetters, in sweltering heat—what is that but baking them alive?

sentences.zh: 在州及所屬刑獄見系罪人，卿可躬親錄問，省略區分。

translations.literal: The prisoners now detained in the prefecture and its subordinate prisons—you should personally examine and question them, simplifying and distinguishing categories.
translations.idiomatic: For every detainee in your prefecture and its subordinate prisons, examine each case yourself, simplifying distinctions and sorting categories.

sentences.zh: 於入務不行者，令俟務開系；

translations.literal: For those who cannot proceed because court is in session, order them to await the opening of sessions and then be detained;
translations.idiomatic: Where court is in recess and proceedings cannot proceed, postpone detention until sessions resume;

sentences.zh: 有理須伸者，速期疏決。

translations.literal: for those with reason who must have their case vindicated, set a swift date for release and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: where a grievance is just and must be redressed, set a swift date for release and judgment.

sentences.zh: 俾皆平允，無至滯淹。

translations.literal: So that all may be fair and equitable, without reaching delay and detention.
translations.idiomatic: See that every case is fair and equitable, and none left to stagnate.

sentences.zh: 又以獄吏逞任情之奸，囚人被非法之苦，宜加檢察，勿縱侵欺。

translations.literal: Moreover, because prison officers indulge whim in villainy and prisoners suffer unlawful affliction, inspection should be increased and indulgence of encroachment and fraud not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Prison officers too often indulge private cruelty while prisoners suffer unlawful abuse—inspect them closely and do not permit extortion or oppression.

sentences.zh: 常令凈掃獄房，洗刷枷匣，知其饑渴，供與水漿，有病者聽骨肉看承，無主者遣醫工救療，勿令非理致斃，以致和氣有傷。

translations.literal: Constantly order clean sweeping of prison cells, washing of cangues and boxes; knowing their hunger and thirst, supply water and gruel; for the ill permit kin to attend; for those without kin dispatch medical officers to save and treat; do not allow death through unreasonable means, causing harm to the harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Keep cells swept clean, wash cangues and restraint boxes, supply water when prisoners hunger or thirst, let families nurse the sick and assign physicians to prisoners without kin, and never let unlawful treatment kill a man and wound the realm's harmonious qi.

sentences.zh: 卿忠幹分憂，仁明蒞事，必能奉詔，體我用心，眷委於茲，興寐無已。

translations.literal: You, loyal and capable in sharing worries, benevolent and discerning in presiding over affairs, surely can obey the edict and embody my intent; your charge in this matter leaves me sleepless whether waking or at rest.
translations.idiomatic: You are loyal, capable, benevolent, and discerning in office—you can surely carry out this edict and grasp my intent. In entrusting you with this charge, my thoughts follow you waking and sleeping.

sentences.zh: 余從敕命處分。」

translations.literal: I await disposition according to the edict command."
translations.idiomatic: I await your disposition as the edict commands."

sentences.zh: 內外官當贖之法，梁、唐皆無定制，多示優容，或因時分輕重。

translations.literal: The law of official commutation for inner and outer officials—Liang and Tang both had no fixed regulation; they mostly showed lenient accommodation, or according to the times distinguished light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Rules for commutations by civil and military officials—under Liang and Tang there was no fixed code; leniency varied with the times and with perceived severity.

sentences.zh: 晉天福六年五月，尚書刑部員外郎李象請：「今後凡是散官，不計高低，若犯罪不得當贖，亦不得上請詳定院覆奏。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the sixth year of Tianfu under Jin, Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments of the Secretariat Li Xiang requested: "From now on, all honorary officials without substantive rank, regardless of high or low, if they commit crimes may not commute nor petition the Review and Verification Office for rehearing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu year 6 (941), Li Xiang, vice director in the Ministry of Punishments, petitioned: "Henceforth every honorary official (san'guan), regardless of grade, who commits a crime shall neither commute sentence nor petition the Review and Verification Office for rehearing.

sentences.zh: 應內外文武官，有品官者自從品官法，無品官有散試官者，應內外帶職廷臣賓從、有功將校等，並請同九品官例。

translations.literal: As for inner and outer civil and military officials: those with ranked offices follow the law for ranked officials; those without ranked office who have honorary trial offices—corresponding to inner and outer officials with concurrent posts as court ministers, retainers, meritorious commanders and the like—should all follow the precedent for ninth-rank officials.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials with substantive ranks should follow ranked-official law; those without rank but holding honorary or trial appointments—including courtiers with concurrent titles, imperial attendants, and meritorious commanders—should all follow the ninth-rank precedent.

sentences.zh: 其京都運巡使及諸道州府衙前職員、內外雜任鎮將等，並請準律，不得上請當贖。

translations.literal: As for the transport and patrol commissioners of the capital and clerks before the gates of prefectures in every circuit, inner and outer miscellaneous appointees, garrison commanders, and the like—all should follow the statutes and may not petition for commutation.
translations.idiomatic: Capital transport and patrol agents, yamen clerks in provincial offices, miscellaneous appointees, and garrison captains should follow the ordinary statutes and may not petition to commute.

sentences.zh: 其巡司馬步司判官，雖有曾歷品官者，亦請同流外職。

translations.literal: As for the judicial officers of circuit horse and foot patrol offices, even if they had once held ranked office, they should also follow outer-stream positions.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial officers of circuit horse and foot patrol offices, even if they had once held substantive rank, should be treated like outer-service posts.

sentences.zh: 準律。

translations.literal: According to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Per the statutory code.

sentences.zh: 杖罪以下，依決罰例，徒罪以上，仍依當贖法。

translations.literal: For crimes of beating-cane and below, follow the precedent for imposed punishment; for exile punishment and above, still follow the commutation law.
translations.idiomatic: For offenses punishable by beating and below, follow ordinary sentencing; for exile and above, commutation law still applies.

sentences.zh: 」至周顯德五年七月，新定《刑統》：「今後定罪，諸道行軍司馬、節度副使、副留守，準從五品官例；

translations.literal: " By the seventh month of the fifth year of Xiande under Zhou, the newly fixed Criminal Compendium: "From now on in sentencing: circuit campaigning marshals, deputy military commissioners, deputy overseers—follow the precedent for fifth-rank adjunct officials;
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xiande year 5 (958), the newly issued Criminal Compendium (Xingtong) fixed sentencing: circuit campaigning marshals, deputy commissioners, and deputy overseers—fifth-rank adjunct precedent;

sentences.zh: 諸道兩使判官、防禦團練副使，準從六品官例；

translations.literal: judicial officers of the two commissioners in every circuit, defense and training vice commissioners—follow the precedent for sixth-rank adjunct officials;
translations.idiomatic: judicial officers to dual commissioners, defense and training vice commissioners—sixth-rank adjunct precedent;

sentences.zh: 節度掌書記、團判官、兩蕃營田等使判官，準從七品官例；

translations.literal: military commission secretaries, group judicial officers, judicial officers of frontier farm commissioners and the like—follow the precedent for seventh-rank adjunct officials;
translations.idiomatic: commission secretaries, regimental judicial officers, and judicial officers of frontier farm commissioners—seventh-rank adjunct precedent;

sentences.zh: 諸道推巡及軍事判官，準從八品官例；

translations.literal: circuit investigation patrol and military judicial officers—follow the precedent for eighth-rank adjunct officials;
translations.idiomatic: circuit investigation patrol and military judicial officers—eighth-rank adjunct precedent;

sentences.zh: 諸軍將校內諸司使、使副、供奉、殿直，臨時奏聽敕旨。

translations.literal: commanders of various armies, commissioners and vice commissioners of inner bureaus, attendants in attendance, palace duty officers—memorialize ad hoc and await edict.
translations.idiomatic: army commanders, inner-bureau commissioners and vice commissioners, palace attendants, and duty officers in the halls—memorialize ad hoc and await imperial decision.

sentences.zh: 」由是內外品官當贖之法，始有定制焉。

translations.literal: " Thus the law of commutation for inner and outer ranked officials first had a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Thus for the first time civil and military officials had a fixed code governing commutation of punishment."
